title: Navigating Posets with Few Maps
summary: We study two new parameters for finite posets motivated by the problem of efficiently determining the set of successors of a given element. A plane map of a poset $P=(X,\leq)$ is an injective mapping of $X$ into the Cartesian plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. Given two different points $a$ and $b$ in the plane, we say that $b$ dominates $a$ if $a<b$ coordinatewise. We say that an element $x$ of $P$ is tight in a plane map $μ$ if the following holds: $x<y$ in $P$ if and only if $μ(y)$ dominates $μ(x)$.
